One possible candidate for *F* is two straight line segments, from (0*,*0) to (1*,a*) and from (1*,a*) to (0*,*1), with *ρ* just sufficient to compensate *d*, such that *e*(0*,*0*,F*(*t*)*,t*) = 0*, ∀t ∈* [0*,*1]. However, for *a <* <u>1</u> 2, this will not be a geodesic: instead, there will be straight lines from (0*,*0) to a point beyond (1*,a*) whose Dirichlet length is greater than the length of *F* to that point. As a result, the geodesic will skip the steeper line segment to (1*,a*) and take such a straight line as a shortcut to *F*, and then follow part of the other line segment to (0*,*1). Similarly, if *a >* 2 <u>1</u>, it will follow part of the line segment from (0*,*0) to (1*,a*) and then shortcut the steep segment to proceed directly to (0*,*1). This suggests that we should try to solve for a metric where the segment from (0*,*0) to (1*,a*) is not skipped by such a shortcut. In other words, we should ask what is the lowest rate metric for which there is a geodesic candidate *F*, so that the distance from (0*,*0) along *F* to any point on *F* is greater than the distance of a shortcut from (0*,*0) to that point.
